Our Programs

Approved training programs, developed in line with international aviation training standards.

Ground School→PPL→Night Rating→CPL→Instrument / Instructor / Multi-engine

Private Pilot Licence (PPL)

The starting point for a career pilot, or for flying as a hobby. About 6 to 8 months, with PPL ground school (10 subjects) and at least 45 hours of flight training in the Cessna 172. You need a valid Student Pilot Licence (SPL) and must be 17 to receive the PPL.

Night Rating

Learn to fly at night relying on instruments. Recommended before or during hour-building. Requires a valid PPL, instrument instruction, night take-offs and landings, a night cross-country flight, theory exam and a skill test.

Instrument Rating

For private or commercial pilots who want to fly in poor weather or at night on instruments. Requires a night rating, instrument flight time, theory exam and a practical test.

Commercial Pilot Licence (CPL)

Required to be paid for flying. You must be 18, hold a Class 1 medical, a valid PPL and a General Radiotelephony Certificate, with at least 200 hours of flight time. CPL ground school lasts 2 months (10 subjects, 75% pass mark).

Instructor Rating

For CPL holders who want to build flight experience quickly towards airline and corporate hiring minimums.

Multi-Engine Rating (Baron 55/58)

An advanced rating to fly aircraft with more than one engine, commonly needed to enter the airline environment.

Ground School / Theory

PPL ground school is 140 hours across 10 subjects, plus 20 hours of flight briefings. CPL ground school runs for 2 months, followed by the examinations.

Aircraft Maintenance Engineer (AME)

A 3-year licence programme in 4 phases: initial theory, on-the-job training at an approved AMO, advanced theory, then on-the-job training and trade testing. Trades: Airframe & Powerplant, Aircraft Structures, Aircraft Instruments, Aircraft Electrics and Aircraft Radios.

Foreign Licence Validation / Conversion

Holders of a foreign licence must apply to the authority before training starts. See NAMCARs/NAMCATs Part 61.01.10 (validation) and 61.01.12 (conversion).

Frequently Asked Questions

Quick answers before you apply.

What are the entry requirements for pilot training?

Be at least 16 to apply for the Student Pilot Licence (SPL), hold a valid Class I or II medical certificate, and have the latest Grade 12 certificate (preferably with English, Mathematics, Physics and Geography) or a relevant tertiary qualification. The PPL needs age 17, the CPL age 18 and a Class 1 medical.

What are the entry requirements for AME training?

Be at least 16 and hold a Namibia Senior Secondary Certificate with five subjects passed (including English, Mathematics and Physical Science) at grade D or better, scoring at least 25 points on the NATA evaluation scale. Mature entry: age 25, 3 years’ relevant work experience, and Grade 10 or an employer’s testimonial. All applicants must pass the NATA Entry Aptitude Test.

What documents do I need to apply?

The completed application form, two passport photos, certified copies of your ID or passport and your school or tertiary certificates, and payment of the non-refundable N$1,000.00 registration fee. Foreign students also need a study visa or proof of application for one.

Where do I get my aviation medical?

An approved Aviation Medical Examiner must do it. Examiners in Windhoek include Dr Estie Maritz (Maerua Mall, 4th Floor, +264 61 254 747), Olympia Medical Centre (+264 61 253 166) and Dr Burger, Van Lill & Bezuidenhout (Pionierspark Medical Centre, +264 61 242 370). Medical aid cards are accepted. Chest X-rays can be done at any approved radiologist.

How much do the courses cost?

Please contact reception at info@nata.com.na or +264 81 141 5140 for the current fees.

How long does training take?

PPL takes about 6 to 8 months. CPL ground school lasts 2 months, followed by exams, and the CPL needs at least 200 hours of flight time. The AME programme takes 3 years.

What happens after I apply?

Reception reviews your application and contacts you. Pilot students then apply for the SPL, pay the initial fees and the N$50,000.00 deposit, and start training.
